channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Dow surges 1,000 points as Democrats take control of Congress
item.description: Stocks jumped on Wednesday morning, just hours after results showed a blue wave.

item.title: US midterm elections: 'Maybe the best colour for Texas is purple'
item.description: Texas flipped blue following the US midterm elections, marking a historic shift for a state that hasn't been led by Democrats in decades. The legacy of prolonged Republican leadership has left a lasting mark, but as Democrat James Talarico said with this election, 'maybe the best colour for Texas is purple.' FRANCE 24's Texas correspondent Andres Espinal reports.

item.title: Election 2026 live results: Speaker Johnson not running for House minority leader
item.description: The winner of the Alaska Senate race has not yet been projected.

item.title: 'Is Republican Party able to pivot away from MAGA movement, or will it sputter forward leaderless?'
item.description: Does an electoral repudiation of Donald Trump also mark the beginning of MAGA’s decline? Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Ian Reifowitz, SUNY Distinguished Professor of Historical Studies at Empire State University, who describes the Republican defeat as “an absolute and complete repudiation” of the president. He connects voters’ economic frustrations with resentment over presidential enrichment, while questioning whether ideological differences between progressive and moderate Democrats proved decisive. Looking towards 2028, Reifowitz identifies a central Republican dilemma: “If JD Vance is the nominee, he can’t run against Donald Trump”, yet Trump himself may refuse to relinquish control of the party.

item.title: French blood banks foil new cyberattack targeting refrigerators
item.description: A cyberattack in France targeted three cold stores containing donated blood samples and plasma, authorities said on Wednesday. The incident – which was unsuccessful due to the facilities' alarm systems – is the latest in a series of suspected attacks that have targeted refrigerators in European supermarkets, as well as French cooperative bank, Credit Mutuel Arkea, which was also affected Wednesday.

item.title: US midterm elections: Gen Z gives Democrats their strongest support
item.description: In the US midterm elections, 50 million members of Gen Z were eligible to vote. Young voters gave Democrats the strongest support, with 75% of them voting for the party. This generation will be the biggest voting bloc in the United States in the coming years. FRANCE 24's Ophelie Jacobson has more.

item.title: How Trump's broken promises on war, inflation handed Democrats the midterms
item.description: Speaking to Fox News following the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump admitted that inflation was likely one reason Republicans did poorly. Many Americans have been frustrated with how the Iran war has pushed up prices, including at the gasoline pump, especially given that Trump had campaigned for his second term on a pledge of “no new wars”, as Ellen Gainsford explains.

item.title: WATCH: What Trump’s next two years with a Democratic Congress could look like
item.description: Chief Washington Correspondent Jon Karl and Chief Global Affairs Correspondent Martha Raddatz break down the major factors that shaped the election, including the war in Iran.

item.title: WATCH: Martin Luther King Jr.'s granddaughter votes for 1st time
item.description: 18-year-old Yolanda Renee King, the granddaughter of Martin Luther King Jr. and Coretta Scott King, has cast a ballot in her very first election in Atlanta.

item.title: Midterms: How Abdul El-Sayed used 'humour and hope' to rebuff racism
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim senator in US history following his midterms victory in Michigan. His victory came despite what he has denounced as racist attacks against him, inlcuding from Donald Trump, which, says FRANCE 24's correspondent Jessica Le Masurier, he rebuffed with a mixture of "humour and hope".

item.title: ABC News Voter Polls explain how Democrats won the US House: Voter Poll analysis
item.description: Democrats are projected to retake the House for the first time since 2020.

item.title: Trump seeks to shift blame but has 'nowhere to hide' after midterms defeat
item.description: Donald Trump has sought to shift the blame for the Republicans' defeat at the midterms by claiming that if he had been on the ballot the party would have won. But the "blue wave" that saw Democrats win control of Congress can be traced directly back to Trump's decisions, says France 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson.

item.title: US Midterms: 'It is now going to be pretty chaotic for Donald Trump'
item.description: The Democrats' victory in the midterm elections have left Donald Trump in a difficult position for the rest of his mandate. The now "blue" House of Representatives will decide the budget, which Trump will have to accept and follow. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Philip Turle has more.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed welcomes Trump's plan to cut Israel aid, calls for end to arms sales
item.description: Michigan's first Muslim senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, discusses his historic victory, an unlikely agreement with Trump on Israel military aid and the political divisions that remain. (Image credit: Salwan Georges)

item.title: Ukrainian's 'not expecting drastic change in US policy' after midterms
item.description: Ukrainians do not expect the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections is change much in regards to US policy on the war with Russia, or at least not quickly, says France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Emmanuelle Chaze. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has not reacted yet to the "blue wave" taking control of Congress in the US.

item.title: A look back at how Trump's political decisions saw his approval rating plummet
item.description: Donald Trump's unpopularity has been cited as a major factor in the Democrats' sweeping victory in the midterms. The latest polls show Trump's approval rating has plummeted to 37.3%, down from 42% in his first midterm election. What were the political decisions that led to such a dramatic decline?

item.title: Blood tests that could spot early signs of cancers to be trialled on thousands of NHS patients
item.description: Blood tests that could spot the early signs of a range of the most common cancers are to be trialled on thousands of NHS patients.

item.title: Blue wave sweeps across America: 'In 1974, we had Watergate babies, now we have Iran War babies'
item.description: Stuart Norval welcomes France 24 International Affairs Editor Philip Turle and Hind Ziane, Geopolitical analyst and founder / CEO of Genpo. "In 1974, we had the Watergate babies. Now we have the Iran War babies," remarks Ziane with this striking historical analogy. Just as the Watergate scandal helped propel a new generation of Democratic lawmakers into Congress in 1974, Zian argues that public disillusionment with the Iran war, mounting economic pressures and dissatisfaction with Donald Trump's leadership may now be reshaping the American political landscape. Yet Turle reminds us, "They're not voting for Democrats because they love the Democrats. They're voting for the Democrats because they don't like Donald Trump."

item.title: Dozens arrested outside court hearing Palestine Action ban challenge
item.description: Dozens of protesters have been arrested outside the Supreme Court ahead of a hearing challenging the ban on Palestine Action.

item.title: The world is reacting to the Democrats' sweeping midterm elections victory
item.description: From Kyiv to Moscow, and Tehran to Tel Aviv, all eyes were on the Democrats big win as foreign powers weigh how a flipped Congress will affect international relations. (Image credit: Allison Robbert)

item.title: Hair and beauty products less regulated than ballpoint pens, say MPs
item.description: Many hair and beauty products are less regulated than ballpoint pens and "people are suffering as a result", MPs have said.

item.title: 'Like a cancer': How data centres became a key issue at midterms
item.description: Over 5,000 data centres are now scattered across the US, some near ubran centes, generating noise pollution and consuming large amount of electricity. Donald Trump has long defended the construction of these mega structures, which are essential for big tech companies to run. But voters, including many Republicans, say they are feeling betrayed by their government.

item.title: Police arrest fourth boy after five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party
item.description: Police have arrested a fourth boy after five teenagers were stabbed at a Halloween party in Chandler's Ford on Saturday.

item.title: Poundland supplier urges 'thorough' state probe into owner's conduct
item.description: A major Poundland supplier has urged the government to "thoroughly investigate" the conduct of its majority owner as the discount chain teeters on the brink of collapse.

item.title: What consequences for Israel as Democrats win the US midterm elections?
item.description: Democrats seized control of the US Congress on Tuesday, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning upset. What are the potential consequences for Israel and Benjamin Netanyahu, as Trump announced on Tuesday that the US will halt $3.8 billion in aid to the country? FRANCE 24's correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky has more.

item.title: US midterms: Trump reacts to the Democrats’ sweeping victory
item.description: US President Donald Trump had rare praise for rival Democrats Tuesday after their stunning US midterm elections victory and admitted the Iran war may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party. But the 80-year-old refused to take any personal responsibility for the result.

item.title: Ethiopia expands hydropower ambitions
item.description: Ethiopia is looking to position itself as an African leader in clean energy, as it prepares to host next year’s COP32 climate summit. Alongside the GERD, the country is building another massive hydropower project on the Omo River in the southwest, as it expands electricity production and exports power to neighbouring countries. This report from our correspondent Tom Canetti.

item.title: From Kansas to Texas, Democrats win big in Republican heartlands
item.description: The Democrats are set to take control of both the House and the Senate following victories in states like South Carolina, Kansas, and Texas, whose switching blue constitutes an historic upset. President Donald Trump has said he will accept the results and blames the candidates themselves for the losses.

item.title: US midterms bring surge of historic firsts for women and minorities
item.description: The 2026 US midterm elections will go down in history for the Democrats' dramatic takeover of both houses of Congress but also for a surge of historic firsts for women, LGBT, Black and Native American candidates, as well as the election of the first Muslim US senator.

item.title: South Korea pushes digital detox for young people addicted to screens
item.description: Back in August, France's Constitutional Council overturned a social media ban for children under 15. Some students, though, are now banned from using their smartphones at school. In South Korea, where an estimated 40 percent of young children and teens are addicted to their mobile devices, authorities are trying to find ways to drastically reduce their screen time – a huge challenge in such a hyper-connected society. FRANCE 24's Chloé Borgnon, Aruna Popuri and Justin McCurry report.

item.title: Midterms: Trump acknowledges role of Iran war, congratulates Dems
item.description: President Donald Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the US-Israeli war on ​Iran ‌played a role in his party's sweeping ⁠defeat in the midterm elections, as Democrats won control of the House of ‌Representatives and the Senate. "I think a part of it ⁠was Iran," Trump told Fox News in an interview in which he also praised the Democrats for their campaign. France 24's Wassim Cornet has more.

item.title: Review: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is superb, streamlined and safe
item.description: Nintendo's new Ocarina of Time remake enshrines its place in the gaming canon for generations to come. But despite its stupendous production values, the game left me feeling oddly bereft. (Image credit: Nintendo)

item.title: Husband invited two men to abuse unconscious wife within an hour, court hears
item.description: (Clockwise) Robert Stewart, Jonathan Kirk, Alan Keelan, Philip Wild, Mohammed Sabir and Jordan Wallace. Pic: PA/Social Media

item.title: US voters back abortion rights and reject Trump's gerrymandering in state ballot measures
item.description: US voters in several states pushed back on President Donald Trump’s redistricting efforts and backed abortion rights in 145 ballot questions during the midterm elections. Some measures put Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to redraw congressional districts, limit reproductive rights and strengthen voter identification requirements.

item.title: Markets react with caution to Democrats' victory in US midterms
item.description: Investors shunned AI stocks and turned to government bonds on Wednesday in the wake of the Democratic Party's takeover of Congress in the US midterm elections. Oil prices meanwhile ticked slightly higher, as uncertainty remains over the direction of US President Donald Trump's war against Iran. Also in this edition, we focus on the central issue of this midterm campaign: the rise in the cost of living.

item.description: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy addressed supporters after ABC News projected Democrat Amy Acton will win the Ohio governor's race.

item.title: WATCH: House Speaker Mike Johnson speaks after Democrats projected to take control of House
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson made remarks after ABC News projected Democrats will win enough seats to take control of the House.

item.title: Champions League: Paris Saint-Germain make easy work of Villarreal
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain made easy work of Villarreal in the Champions League (6-0). The game was decided after 17 minutes and four goals.

item.title: DR Congo residents sue Chinese mining giant for widespread pollution
item.description: In Kolwezi, the mining capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, local residents are suing a huge Chinese mine and the government for environmental pollution. It will be one of the most important cases the country has seen. FRANCE 24's correspondent Emmet Livingstone reports.

item.title: 30 million South Africans registered to vote across nine provinces
item.description: In South Africa, around 30 million people have registered to cast their votes across the country's nine provinces. The economy is at the forefront of the November 4 local elections. The spotlight is on Gauteng, a province long plagued by governance challenges. FRANCE 24's correspondent Eunice Masson reports.

item.title: Trans row nurse Sandie Peggie appeals tribunal ruling
item.description: Nurse Sandie Peggie will appeal against a ruling by an employment tribunal that a nursing union did not discriminate against her because of her beliefs about gender, her legal team has said.

item.title: US Marine dies after training incident in Japan, officials say
item.description: The incident is under investigation, the Marines said.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House
item.description: As speaker, the New York Democrat would be second in the presidential line of succession, after the vice president. He has vowed to focus on affordability and holding the administration accountable. (Image credit: Alex Wong)

item.title: These 10 candidates for governor made history in the 2026 election
item.description: Voters on Tuesday elected the nation's first Black woman governor and the nation's first Native American woman governor. (Image credit: Brynn Anderson/AP, Sam Wasson/Getty Images, Jacquelyn Martin/AP)

item.title: Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford beats Republican incumbent for governor
item.description: Democrat Aaron Ford defeated Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo. He's set to become Nevada's first Black governor. (Image credit: Ethan Miller)

item.description: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms addressed supporters after ABC News projected her the winner of the Georgia governor's race, making her the first Black female governor in the history of the U.S.

item.description: Australia's landmark social media ban for under-16s faces challenges in court over accusations that it amounts to censorship and creates privacy issues.

item.title: Bomb threats reported on multiple flights, including two from UK airports
item.description: At least seven flights, including two from the UK, have been affected by bomb threats, which caused unplanned landings and temporary airport closures.

item.description: Students at Howell High School filled their football field with over a quarter million pounds of food for the nonprofit, Dermer Dreams. David Muir reports on the volunteers that delivered.

item.description: A British adventurer who has been walking around the world for almost three decades returned to his childhood home Monday.

item.description: Tenerife football player Jesus de Miguel has died after suffering a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision in a match on Monday.

item.description: Three customers and two employees at a Chili's restaurant suffered chemical burns after an employee mistakenly used a cleaning powder instead of sugar to make the drinks, health officials say.

item.description: The US military has carried out "limited strikes" on Qeshm Island in Iran - hours before the midterms are due to take place.

item.description: British troops will be allowed to fire back at Russian forces if attacked as part of a multinational mission to secure any future peace in Ukraine, Western officials have said.
